# v0.0.1

First tagged release of goc, a self-contained C-subset compiler written in
pure Go. No libc, no external toolchain: goc compiles one translation unit
straight to a Windows PE32+ or Linux ELF64 executable via its own assembler
(goa). The runtime (goclib) is embedded C that is compiled on demand.

## Highlights

- C89 baseline plus struct/union/enum/bitfields/_Bool/const, function
  pointers, multi-dimensional arrays, float/double, brace-init, switch,
  do-while, goto, variadic builtins, typedef and UFCS-style methods
  (`a.add(x)` → `int_array_add(a, len, x)`)
- Built-in `print()` for scalars and arrays (`[1, 2, 3]`), with a shared
  runtime skeleton and per-type converters
- Optimizing passes at `-O1+`: inlining, constant propagation, peephole,
  dead-store elimination and liveness-based dead code elimination; `-O0`
  output is byte-identical to the unoptimized pipeline
- `printf` family, string/memory functions, ctype and a small stdlib, all
  shipped as compilable C (no assembly in the runtime)
- gcc/clang-compatible CLI (`-c -S -E -o -D -I -target linux` …), works as a
  drop-in `cc` for build scripts
- Windows (kernel32) and Linux (raw syscalls) targets; the Linux leg is
  validated on a real kernel in CI

## Assets

Each release is a drop-in toolchain folder: grab the two binaries for your
platform and put them in one directory — goc finds goa **next to its own
executable**, so it just works (this is why the filenames carry no version).

- Windows: `goc.exe`, `cc.exe` (gcc-compatible alias of the compiler),
  `goa.exe` (assembler backend)
- Linux: `goc`, `goa` (bare names, cross-built ELF64)
- `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `SHA256SUMS.txt` — checksums for all assets

## Notes

This is a single-pass compiler over a C subset; it intentionally does not
implement C99+ (VLA, `long long`, `_Generic`, …) or file I/O / math.h.
`printf` width specifiers are ignored (`%.Nf` precision on `%f`/`%g` works).
